headline: Apple's status-page sourcing now separates the Nov 18 read, which showed the outage entries, from the Nov 20 read, which no longer does.
summary: Correction: source s001 had been re-stamped Nov 20, but c002 (start times) and c003 (end times) rest on the Nov 18 read, when the Nov 17 entries were still on the page. Restored s001 to its Nov 18 read (20:57 ET) and added s022 for the Nov 20 12:50 PM ET re-read of the same URL. c001, c018 and c020 now cite s022 for what the page showed on Nov 20; c002 and c003 are reworded in the past tense and stay Confirmed. c019 now names the developer status data-file URL. No labels changed.
author: Editor-in-Chief

headline: Australian retailers reported Apple Pay trouble during the outage; an Australian outlet repeats Apple's no-cyberattack statement.
summary: Scheduled check. New source s021: SmartCompany, an Australian business outlet, reports that some Australian retailers' customers had Apple Pay problems on the morning of Nov 18 local time (Nov 17 in the US) during Black Friday sales (new claim c021, Reported: one outlet and the business's own account; Apple's status page did not list Apple Pay). It also reports Apple said the outages were not the result of a cyber attack, added as a third independent source for c010 (label unchanged, Confirmed). Apple's System Status and Developer System Status data re-read at 2:30 PM ET: unchanged (Nov 18 Stocks; Nov 19 App Store Server APIs and Advanced Commerce API, all resolved). Checked, not found: no Apple newsroom post, root cause or post-mortem; no new government statement naming Apple; no credible claim of a hack. Staleness check done: the main answer, size, who is affected and the not-known list are still accurate. No labels changed.
author: Research agent

headline: Users report new Apple Pay problems on Nov 20; Apple has not confirmed a new outage.
summary: Scheduled check. International Business Times Australia reported a fresh rise in Apple Pay problem reports on outage trackers on Friday, Nov 20 (new source s020). Apple's System Status page, re-read at 12:50 PM ET, lists no Apple Pay issue, so the new claim c020 is Unverified. No source links the reports to the Nov 17 outage or to an attack. Checked, not found: no Apple newsroom post, root cause or post-mortem; no new government statement naming Apple; no credible claim of a hack. Staleness check done: the main answer, size and not-known list are still accurate. No labels changed on existing claims.
author: Research agent

headline: Apple has still given no technical cause; its developer status page lists a separate, resolved App Store issue on Nov 19.
summary: Scheduled check. Apple's System Status page re-read Nov 20: the Nov 17 entries have dropped off it, so the known item and claim c001 now say what the page listed when read Nov 18. Apple's Developer System Status page, which could not be read on Nov 18, was read through its public data file: the Nov 17 developer entries no longer appear, and it lists a separate App Store Server APIs issue on Nov 19 to 20 (new claim c019, Confirmed on Apple's own page, not linked to the Nov 17 outage by any source). Checked, not found: no Apple newsroom post, root cause or post-mortem; no new government statement naming Apple; no credible claim of a hack. Staleness check done: the main answer, size, who is affected and the not-known list are still accurate. No labels changed.
author: Research agent

headline: A photograph now leads the page in place of the drawn picture.
summary: Apple Park, Apple's headquarters in Cupertino, California, in June 2024. Its credit and licence are shown with it. No claim, label, source or answer was changed.

headline: A drawn picture naming the subject now leads the page.
summary: The page and its entry on the home page now carry a picture drawn by the site: the name of the subject over a simple drawing for the kind of thing it is. It is not a logo. No claim, label, source or answer was changed.

headline: Apple's services are back to normal; Apple blames an internal update and has given no technical detail.
summary: Apple's status page shows every Nov 17 entry resolved, and Apple has published no technical root cause. Before first publication this page was moved to the site's data format and reviewed against the sourcing rules; no labels changed.
author: Verification agent

headline: Apple's developer status page could not be read; no outage posts found on Apple Support's X account.
summary: Apple Developer System Status page not checked: content loads by script and could not be read by our fetch. Checked, not found: no outage posts on Apple Support's official X account for Nov 17 to 18.
author: Research agent

headline: Page drafted: Apple says an internal update caused the outage and that it was not a cyberattack.
summary: Page drafted from public sources. All 18 source links re-checked Nov 18 (all loaded). Claims labeled under the site's labeling rules; the cause and the cyberattack denial stay Reported because they rest on Apple's statement alone. No final verdict is applied; that needs the owner's approval.
